operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers everywhere: table "member", columns "Member_ID", "Performance_ID", "Date", "Name" — must be double-quoted in generated SQL.

FK child column types contradict parent PK types: member_attendance.Member_ID is INT but member.Member_ID is TEXT (values '1','2',...); member_attendance.Performance_ID INT vs performance.Performance_ID REAL (1.0).
member.Member_ID is TEXT storing integer-looking strings; TS String fuzzer will emit non-numeric strings, breaking FK join semantics vs INT child.
performance.Performance_ID declared REAL, storage real, values 1.0..6.0 — Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) will emit floats; PK uniqueness filtering must handle float equality.
performance.Date is TEXT storing 'February 2' style (month-name, no year, no zero-pad) — declared type dispatches to String fuzzer, NOT Date; TS will not produce date-like values.
member_attendance has composite PK (Member_ID, Performance_ID) — both members get max_l0=30 cap; sample_fresh_primary_keys must dedupe on the tuple.
member_attendance.Member_ID distinct=7 but member has 11 rows; Performance_ID distinct=5 but performance has 6 rows — FK coverage is partial, not full.
All tables tiny (11/6/8 rows); original_values sampling k=min(5,len) will draw nearly the whole column, so element reuse dominates over fresh draws.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs; no views/triggers; no self-FKs; no dangling FKs; no missing parents.
member.Name has accented chars (González, Héctor, Campana) — String CHARSET a-zA-Z0-9() will not reproduce them; literal pool from train SQL may carry them.
member.Role and Nationality are low-cardinality enums (5 and 3 distinct) — String fuzzer will emit random strings, destroying the enum.
performance.Host and Location are proper-noun strings (team/arena names) — String fuzzer emits random charset strings, not plausible names.
operator_ts_expectations: member.Member_ID (TEXT, PK): String fuzzer, single-col PK -> max_l0=inf, fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() length 0..20; PK dedupe keeps first occurrence; values like '1','10' from originals mixed with random junk.
member.Name/Nationality/Role: String fuzzer, random charset strings + contaminate; enum/name structure lost -> FN on queries filtering Nationality='Uruguay' or Role='Violin'.
performance.Performance_ID (REAL, PK): Number fuzzer, scale from 'real' (no args -> default), int=False; emits floats in [-10^s,10^s] perturbed by +-0.01/0.02; PK dedupe on floats.
performance.Date (TEXT): String fuzzer, NOT Date fuzzer — TS will never emit 'February N' format; queries comparing Date strings will mostly miss -> FN.

performance.Attendance (INT): Number fuzzer int=True, perturb +-1/+-2; range from originals [165,2173] but list_max overwritten to full 10^scale -> implausible huge/negative attendances -> FN on range predicates.

member_attendance.Member_ID/Performance_ID (INT, FK): filled from parent's FINAL filtered column with replacement; parent member.Member_ID is TEXT strings, child INT — sqlite affinity coerces on insert, but join semantics may still work via text->int coercion.
member_attendance.Num_of_Pieces (INT): Number fuzzer, small range from originals [1,4] but list_max overwritten -> large values -> FN on 'Num_of_Pieces > 2' style.
Composite PK dedupe on (Member_ID, Performance_ID) after FK fill: with replacement draws from 11 and 6 parents, many duplicate pairs dropped -> small final table, possibly empty if parents empty.
FK fill draws from parent's final column AFTER parent PK/unique filtering; if parent table ends up empty (all rows dropped), child gets NULLs -> join queries return empty -> FN.

p=0.2 default, whole-instance p=0 w.p. 0.3: in p=0 instances all columns return elements (original/pool values) -> near-copy of original, few kills; in p=0.2 instances heavy contamination -> many implausible values.
String contaminate (suffix/prefix/drop-char) on Member_ID and Name breaks equality joins and LIKE patterns -> FN on exact-match and prefix queries.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers dispatched on this DB (no such declared types) — TS misses here are purely String/Number implausibility, not date-format issues.
